 During public meeting in Parliament: Prime Minister Mike Eman imposes a minimum wage increase without genuine dialogue with the commercial sector and the community 
 Local/Aruba English During public meeting in Parliament: Prime Minister Mike Eman imposes a minimum wage increase without genuine dialogue with the commercial sector and the community
 by EA News Author November 8, 2026 0 8090 
 Share 0 
 During a recent session in the Parliament of Aruba, Prime Minister Mike Eman, along with his fellow ministers, participated in the discussion regarding the modification of the 2026 Budget and other unfinished legislative projects. With a speech in which he declared that “the discussion about a fair wage can no longer be postponed,” Eman pretended to be open to consultation. However, the reality is that the prime minister shows no interest in a genuine dialogue; he pretended to have consulted while doing nothing substantial, showing up to dictate a minimum wage hike with direct consequences that will ultimately affect the people themselves.
 Below are the key points presented and their direct consequences:
 Pretension of dialogue and imposition of wage increase 
 Point presented: Prime Minister Eman presented a chronology of requests for advice and invitations sent to commercial associations, claiming that the time has come to make decisions and that the minimum wage must be brought closer to the existence minimum ( bestaansminimum ) in three phases.
 Consecuencia: Contrary to what is spent to project a participatory process, the attitude of imposing and dictating a wage increase without reaching a real consensus with the private sector creates instability. Without structural dialogue and true negotiation, the people will ultimately be affected by a higher cost of life and labor uncertainty, as businesses were not properly listened to in order to absorb this change.
 Minimum wage increase vs. Cost of living and inflation 
 Point presented: Eman referred to research by the Economisch Bureau Amsterdam (EBA), stating that inflation in Aruba is better explained by imports and that a wage increase would not have a significant effect on general prices.
 Consecuencia: If the minimum wage increase is imposed without control measures and structural support, the risk is that businesses’ operational costs will suddenly spike. This could mean a “direct effect” where merchants transfer this expense into the final price of products and services, further reducing the purchasing power that was intended to be improved.
 Impact on small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) 
 Punto presentado: The government mentioned the need to identify relief measures for small and medium-sized enterprises that depend heavily on labor.
 Consecuencia: In the current framework, if government relief remains mere talk and is not implemented immediately alongside the wage increase, the consequences for SMEs could be drastic: reduction of working hours, freezing of new vacancies, or, in worst-case scenarios, staff cuts (unemployment) just to keep doors open.
 Economic growth and the “shadow side of Aruba” ( Schaduwkant van Aruba ) 
 Punto presented: Referring to the report De schaduwkant van Aruba , the Prime Minister noted that the country’s and tourism’s prosperity has not reached every family, and that purchasing power must be improved and poverty combated.
 Consecuencia: The attempt to solve this inequality solely through a wage mandate, without addressing the underlying problems in the economy (such as energy costs, high taxes, and bureaucracy), creates a false sense of relief for the worker. If purchasing power is devoured by higher prices at the supermarket, the social and economic inequality gap will continue to widen.
 Investment proposal vs. Economic risk 
 Punto presented: Eman stipulated that the increase must be viewed as an investment in purchasing power and quality of life that will stimulate the local economy, citing the experiences of Bonaire and Saba as references.
 Consecuencia: Although an increase in wages may bring short-term relief to minimum-income families, the lack of an comprehensive plan with the commercial sector can lead to a slowdown in overall economic growth. Aruba’s reality differs from the BES islands, and a dictated decision can undermine private sector investor confidence and even cause many merchants to leave Aruba.
 Conclusion Although the declared intention in Parliament is to connect economic growth with the improvement of quality of life, the guise under which this proposal was presented remains a unilateral dictate. The lack of interest in true dialogue on the part of Prime Minister Mike Eman leaves the people at risk of suffering the negative economic consequences of these measures in their daily lives.
